body:
## Why

A day's schedule puts any wait before a stop's set time before the drive to it. On a day whose first selected stop has a set time, that puts the wait before the day's first drive. So the schedule says to leave hours after the day's start time, and shows the free time where the party slept, or at home. That goes against the rule in domain model 4.1: "On a day with a leg, the party leaves where it slept at that time." The start time is when the user said they want to leave. The coordinator reads this same schedule (`read_itinerary`), so it can pass a wrong departure time on to the user.

Waits later in the day stay before the drive, where the party is. Free time is time nothing is planned for, worked out from the gap before a set time. When the party does something specific with it, such as checking in at the hotel or walking around town, that's a stop. #169 adds a stop for checking in at the stay, and with this rule, the free time after a check-in shows at the hotel, before the drive out.

## What happened

Live site, session `session_5hf47qpn` (the Natick to Bar Harbor trip). Day 1 starts at 10:00 a.m. Its only selected stop is the College of the Atlantic alumni event, set for 6:00 p.m. A lunch stop along the leg has no place yet, so it takes no time. The drive is 5 h 25 m with the buffer. The itinerary view shows:

- 10:00 a.m. to 12:35 p.m.: free time, 2 h 35 m.
- 12:35 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.: drive.
- 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.: the event.

It should show the drive from 10:00 a.m. to 3:25 p.m., then free time from 3:25 to 6:00 p.m., then the event.

## Where it comes from

Domain model 4.1, "How the schedule is worked out": "The party waits before driving, not after, so the wait shows as free time before the drive." The code is `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`, which works each drive's start back from the arrival. Arrival times don't change with this issue, so the late check, the opening hours check, and the other check results stay the same (technical spec section 8). Only where the first drive and its free time sit in the schedule changes.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out, including the stops with no selected place).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's itinerary section, which says what free time is).

## Open questions

None.

## Do

- **The day's first drive leaves at the day's start time.** When the party arrives before the first selected stop's set time, the wait shows as free time after that drive, before the stop. Every later wait stays as it is: free time before the drive on. Change `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`.
- **A stop with no selected place still goes where its time falls,** so the schedule stays in time order. When its set time falls within the free time after the first drive, it splits that free time. Work out where one goes when its time falls during that drive, and say so in domain model 4.1.
- Change domain model 4.1 to match, and check that its examples still hold.
- Change the coordinator's line "Free time is a wait before the party drives on" in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and technical spec 5.2 if it says the same. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Add a schedule test for a day like Day 1 above, and change any existing ones that this changes. Tests use fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A test shows a day like Day 1 above: the drive starts at the day's start time, and the free time comes after it, before the set time.
- A test shows a later wait in the day still comes before the drive on.
- Check results for the same trip are unchanged.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR.

## Why

A day's schedule puts the wait before a stop's set time as free time before the drive, so the party leaves at the last minute. On a day that starts with that wait, the schedule says to leave hours after the day's start time, and shows the free time where the party slept, or at home. That goes against the rule just above it in domain model 4.1: "On a day with a leg, the party leaves where it slept at that time." The coordinator reads this same schedule (`read_itinerary`), so it can pass a wrong departure time on to the user. Drive times are averages, so a schedule that leaves at the last minute is late whenever traffic is bad, while one that arrives early and waits is the safer plan to show.

## What happened

Live site, session `session_5hf47qpn` (the Natick to Bar Harbor trip). Day 1 starts at 10:00 a.m. Its only selected stop is the College of the Atlantic alumni event, set for 6:00 p.m. A lunch stop along the leg has no place yet, so it takes no time. The drive is 5 h 25 m with the buffer. The itinerary view shows:

- 10:00 a.m. to 12:35 p.m.: free time, 2 h 35 m.
- 12:35 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.: drive.
- 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.: the event.

It should show the drive from 10:00 a.m. to 3:25 p.m., then free time from 3:25 to 6:00 p.m., then the event.

## Where it comes from

Domain model 4.1, "How the schedule is worked out": "The party waits before driving, not after, so the wait shows as free time before the drive." The code is `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`, which works the drive's start back from the arrival. Arrival times don't change with this issue, so the late check, the opening hours check, and the other check results stay the same (technical spec section 8). Only where the drive and the free time sit in the schedule changes.

## Design

- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.1 (how the schedule is worked out, including the Moab Day 4 example and the stops with no selected place).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (the coordinator's itinerary section, which says what free time is).
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), section 9 (the itinerary view).

## Open questions

None.

## Do

- **The party drives on as soon as it can, and waits after the drive.** Each drive starts when the item before it ends, or at the day's start time. When the party arrives before a stop's set time, the wait shows as free time after the drive, before the stop. Change `#addSelected()` in `src/domain/day-timeline.ts`.
- **A stop with no selected place still goes where its time falls,** so the schedule stays in time order. When its set time falls within the free time after the drive, it splits that free time. Work out where one goes when its time falls during the drive, and say so in domain model 4.1.
- Change domain model 4.1 to match, including its examples: the Moab Day 4 stargazing example, and the San Francisco Day 2 and Moab Day 2 examples of stops with no selected place.
- Change the coordinator's line "Free time is a wait before the party drives on" in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`, and technical spec 5.2 if it says the same. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with the change.
- Change the schedule tests to match, and add one for a day that starts with a wait, like Day 1 above. Tests use fakes (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).

## Done when

- A test shows a day like Day 1 above: the drive starts at the day's start time, and the free time comes after it, before the set time.
- Check results for the same trip are unchanged.
- `npm run check` passes.

A PR.
